run.question: Three days ago, on 2026-11-20 between 15:15 and 16:15 UTC, our billing service logged errors during invoice export. Search the Elasticsearch index cp1-billing-logs for ERROR entries from service billing in that window and tell me what failed and how many errors there were.

report.summary: The billing log search is answered: in cp1-billing-logs between 2026-11-20T15:15:00Z and 2026-11-20T16:15:00Z there are exactly 40 ERROR documents, all with service=billing, and every one is the same failure — 'invoice export failed: upstream ledger-api returned HTTP 503 (batch NNNN)' — with batch numbers running 1000 to 1039, the first at 15:15:11Z and the last at 16:13:41Z, roughly every 90 seconds so that every 5-minute bucket in the window holds 3–4 errors. The failing operation is therefore the invoice export batch job in billing, and the failure it reports is an HTTP 503 from its upstream dependency ledger-api. What remains unresolved is the state of ledger-api itself: in this Run the Jaeger trace source and the Prometheus metrics source both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, and the log index carries no ledger-api logs, so the 503 is known only from billing's own message and cannot be corroborated against the dependency's own telemetry; no ledger-api or billing Kubernetes Service/ConfigMap was returned either. The index also contains no documents before 2026-11-20T15:15:11, so when the failures began is unknown. Outside the incident the same index shows only 20 INFO 'invoice export completed' entries on 2026-11-23, i.e. later successful exports, and no ERROR documents on 2026-11-21, 2026-11-22 or 2026-11-23.

claims.text: In cp1-billing-logs, the query {level:"ERROR" AND service:"billing"} over 2026-11-20T15:15:00Z–2026-11-20T16:15:00Z returned total 40 (relation eq); the by_level aggregation contains only the key ERROR with doc_count 40 and the by_service aggregation only the key billing with doc_count 40, with sum_other_doc_count 0 for both.

All 40 returned ERROR documents carry the message form 'invoice export failed: upstream ledger-api returned HTTP 503 (batch NNNN)', with sequential batch numbers 1000 through 1039; the earliest is 2026-11-20T15:15:11Z (batch 1000) and the latest 2026-11-20T16:13:41Z (batch 1039), one entry roughly every 90 seconds, so the failing operation is the billing invoice export and the reported failure is HTTP 503 from upstream ledger-api.

A 5-minute date_histogram over the same ERROR+billing query shows errors in every bucket of the window: 15:15 (4), 15:20 (3), 15:25 (3), 15:30 (4), 15:35 (3), 15:40 (3), 15:45 (4), 15:50 (3), 15:55 (3), 16:00 (4), 16:05 (3), 16:10 (3); source_start_at 2026-11-20T15:15:11Z and source_end_at 2026-11-20T16:13:41Z.

Across the whole authorized window the cp1-billing-logs index holds 60 documents, all with service=billing: a daily histogram returns 40 ERROR documents on 2026-11-20, 0 on 2026-11-21, 0 on 2026-11-22 and 20 INFO documents on 2026-11-23; the earliest document in the index is 2026-11-20T15:15:11Z.

The 20 non-incident documents are service=billing, level=INFO, message 'invoice export completed (batch NNNN)' with batch numbers 2019 down to 2000, timestamps from 2026-11-23T14:17:11Z to 2026-11-23T15:14:11Z, showing invoice exports completing again on that later date.

The immediate cause of the invoice-export failures is the upstream dependency ledger-api being unavailable or returning 503 for the duration of the window; this rests only on billing's own log text, since no ledger-api spans, metrics, logs or Kubernetes objects were observed in this Run, and the specific reason for the 503 (overload, restart, upstream outage) is unverified.

Within the index's own coverage, the failure is not continuous: no ERROR documents exist on 2026-11-21, 2026-11-22 or 2026-11-23, and 2026-11-23 shows only INFO 'invoice export completed' entries, so the condition that produced the 40 errors is not evidenced after 2026-11-20T16:13:41Z in this index.

Rejected as far as this index goes: a second, differently worded billing error class or another service logging errors in the same window. The by_level and by_service aggregations for the ERROR+billing query returned only ERROR/billing with sum_other_doc_count 0, and all 40 documents shown are the same invoice-export/ledger-api 503 message; no other error text was returned by the sampled queries.

To find why ledger-api returned 503, inspect ledger-api's own telemetry and logs (server-side HTTP status, pod restarts/OOMKilled, deployment rollout) for 2026-11-20 15:15–16:15 UTC; that data is not present in cp1-billing-logs and was not reachable in this Run.

gaps: Jaeger traces were not queried successfully: traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE twice, so no span-level view of billing or ledger-api call chains exists in this Run.

Prometheus metrics were not queried successfully: get_metric_names for {__name__=~".*ledger.*|.*billing.*"} returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE twice, so any ledger-api or billing ERROR/error-rate, HTTP status or latency series are unknown rather than zero.

No ledger-api identity was observed: no spans, logs, metric labels or Kubernetes objects for ledger-api were returned; queries for Services matching ledger|billing and for ConfigMaps mentioning ledger returned no_data (empty), which shows only that those queries matched nothing, not that the dependency is absent.

cp1-billing-logs contains no documents at all before 2026-11-20T15:15:11Z, so whether the invoice-export failures started earlier than 15:15 and how long they lasted after 16:15 is unknown; the 16:15 boundary of the requested window is not shown to be the end of the incident.
cp1-replicated exists but holds 0 documents, so it contributes no evidence.
The reason for the HTTP 503 (ledger-api restart, resource exhaustion, network policy, or other) cannot be determined from billing's log text alone.
No change history source is integrated, so any configuration or deployment change preceding 2026-11-20T15:15 cannot be checked.
next_steps: Pull ledger-api application and access logs for 2026-11-20 15:15–16:15 UTC from its own log index or pod logs to confirm the 503s and their reason.
Check ledger-api pod status, container last termination reason/exit code and events for the same window (restart, OOMKilled, probe failure) to distinguish unavailability from overload.
Review ledger-api request-rate, error-rate and latency metrics over 2026-11-20 around 15:15 to see when the 503s started and whether they were capacity-related.
Confirm whether invoice export batches 1000–1039 were retried and how the later batch-2000 series on 2026-11-23 relates to the failed batches.
